summary: Published node2's private (lan) app on TCP/8080 through node1 to node3 using Ansible, without giving node3 any other access to the lan network. Bootstrapped SSH trust (user "antrieb", node4's existing keypair) on node1/node2/node3, wrote /root/inventory.ini and /root/port-forward.yml on the ansible-controller (node4), and ran it via the required /root/run.sh + EXECUTED_FILE entrypoint. The playbook: (1) on node1 (VyOS) sets eth1=10.50.50.1/24, a destination-NAT rule redirecting eth0:tcp/8080 to node2's lan IP (10.50.50.2:8080), a source-NAT/masquerade rule for that specific flow (needed because node2 is dual-homed and would otherwise reply directly to node3, bypassing node1), and a default-drop forward filter that only allows established/related plus that one 8080 flow; (2) on node2 statically addresses eth1, deploys a small systemd-managed Python http.server as the demo app, and uses firewalld to allow 8080 only in the "internal" zone bound to eth1 (explicitly disabled on the public/mgmt zone); (3) verifies from node3 via the uri module that the app is reachable only through node1 and that direct access to node2's lan IP fails. Caught and fixed two real bugs during testing: `set -e` silently aborting the VyOS script-template sourcing under Ansible's shell module (empty output, instant rc=1), and NetworkManager resetting eth1's firewalld zone to "public" on every boot — fixed by pinning connection.zone=internal on the nmcli connection profile; without that fix the forward would have silently broken after the very first reboot. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all four nodes one at a time (node3, node4, node2, node1 — with node2 rebooted twice to confirm the zone-persistence fix), each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of services/config, with the port-forward re-verified end-to-end after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology via exec: node1=VyOS router (eth0=mgmt/dhcp, eth1=lan/no-dhcp), node2=AlmaLinux9 app host (same two NICs), node3=AlmaLinux9 client (mgmt-only), node4=Ubuntu ansible-controller (mgmt-only)
Bootstrapped SSH trust: created 'antrieb' user + sudoers on node2/node3, added a matching VyOS login user with public-key auth on node1, all keyed to node4's existing ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub
Verified ansible connectivity to all three managed hosts from node4 (ansible ping)
Debugged and fixed 'set -e' breaking VyOS script-template sourcing under ansible.builtin.shell
Fixed 'show firewall ipv4 forward filter rules' invalid VyOS op-mode syntax to 'show firewall'
Ran playbook via EXECUTED_FILE=/root/port-forward.yml /root/run.sh: configured node1 NAT/firewall, deployed+started webapp.service and firewalld rules on node2, and validated end-to-end from node3
Found NetworkManager resets eth1's firewalld zone to public on reboot; fixed by adding zone: internal to the nmcli task and re-ran the playbook
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, config, service status) on all four nodes
Restarted node3, node4, node2 (x2, to confirm the zone-persistence fix), and node1 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until exec access returned

Verified changed boot_id and full functional recovery (NAT/firewall/interfaces on node1, webapp+firewalld+zone on node2, forward reachability + private-network isolation from node3) after every restart
